Subject: Partner adapter & hybrid vector-tiering: tech checklist and next steps

Thanks all — looping in the team on the multi-partner POC we discussed. High level: Redwood will validate two integration patterns for customers who want a hybrid vector tiering strategy (hot: Pinecone/Weaviate, cold: S3/pgvector snapshots) and produce a short playbook for partner docs and the Redwood Console UI options.

Can each partner confirm these three items by end of week?
- Upsert / query QPS targets you support and any batching recommendations
- Index/schema constraints (vector dims, metadata limits, namespace semantics)
- Snapshot/restore flow to/from S3 (format, ACLs, cost considerations)

I've attached a lightweight POC-Requirements spreadsheet with sample workloads. Proposed timeline: technical alignment call next Tue (05/11), week-long PoC (internal), results and playbook by 05/20.

If any blockers (billing, NDA, or export controls), flag here.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec | Redwood Inference

Attachments: POC-Requirements.xlsx (sheet: workloads + acceptance criteria)

From: Andrew Xu <andrew@pinecone.io>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partner adapter & hybrid vector-tiering: tech checklist and next steps

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the clear checklist. Quick answers from Pinecone side:
- Throughput: we can sustain steady-state 500 qps with 3 replica configuration for 128-d vectors; burst to 2k qps with autoscaling. Batch upserts of 1k vectors are recommended for cost efficiency.
- Index constraints: vector dims supported up to 2048; metadata per record currently 2KB recommended. Namespaces map cleanly to tenants, we prefer explicit namespace per customer.
- Snapshots: we support exports to S3 via our managed export tool (Parquet with vector payloads). We need an IAM role with PutObject and ListBucket.

Two asks:
1) Can you share expected mean sequence length and average vector dim for the PoC workloads (sheet may help).
2) For cold-tiering, do you expect reads-through from cold -> hot on miss, or an async prefetch? That changes latency/SLA targets.

I'll join the Tue call.

Andrew
Partner Eng, Pinecone

Adding a couple product/ops notes for the PoC acceptance criteria:
- We need a sub-100ms 95th-percentile retrieval latency from the hot tier for chat use-cases; for archived cold reads we can accept up to 500ms if async.
- Cost measurement: tokenize call volumes + vector ops separately; please provide cost-per-1M-queries and cost-per-1M-upserts estimates for the config used.
- Backup / retention: we require a snapshot cadence (daily) and a retention TTL of 90 days for the PoC.

SLA draft will need minor edits — Karthik, flagged a section about maintenance windows that we should discuss with partners on the call.

Marissa
Head of Product, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Andrew. I've updated the POC spreadsheet with our sample payloads and average vector dims (doc: 512 dims for semantic embeddings; additional feature vectors at 64 dims). Key engineering clarifications we need from partners pre-call:
- Upsert idempotency guarantees and recommended vector versioning strategy (we version client-side but want to understand server-side behavior on collisions).
- How tombstones / deletes are propagated to snapshots (soft delete vs hard delete semantics).
- Expected consistency model for new writes (eventual vs strong) — this impacts cache invalidation inside Redwood runtime.

Attached: POC-Requirements.xlsx (sheet: sample_payloads).

Forwarding from the Weaviate infra team with a couple notes:
- Weaviate supports hybrid storage via our S3-blob connector; we persist vectors and metadata into the vector index and optionally write chunked snapshots to S3 (we recommend AVRO/Parquet for durability).
- Compatibility: we can accept pgvector dumps via migration tooling, but index tuning is required (we can provide recommended HNSW params).

Attaching a short SLA-draft.pdf for consideration — it contains maintenance windows and expected RTO for cross-tier restores.
